overview.overview:
South Carolina sits well to the right of the nation, having voted Republican by about 12 points in 2020 and roughly 18 points in 2024. The forecast expects a Republican margin of about 11 points, reflecting a national environment that favors Democrats by nearly 5 points on the generic ballot. Even with that tailwind, the state's underlying lean of more than 16 points toward the GOP keeps it firmly in the Republican column.

With 9 electoral votes and essentially no chance of being the tipping-point state, South Carolina is not expected to be competitive. No state polls are available, so the projection rests on recent results and the national picture.
overview.watch: A substantially stronger-than-expected Democratic national wave, beyond the current generic ballot edge, would be needed to bring South Carolina into play.
key_factors: A strong Republican lean built on double-digit margins in 2020 and 2024
A favorable national environment for Democrats that narrows, but does not close, the gap
Nikki Haley's presence on the Republican ticket as a home-state figure could reinforce the GOP advantage
